prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: B014 as a sole prize part, with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. I have tested it against the strongest objections from the first round and it holds. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model identified one transparent mechanism, interlayer tunnelling that suppresses the Dirac velocity at a magic angle. The 2018 experiments then found correlated insulators and superconductivity in a system tuned by a gate and a twist angle. The theory predicted the flat band and not those phases, so the experimental discovery is a genuine step into a new regime and not a confirmation. The phases have since been seen by many groups with transport, scanning-probe and compressibility measurements, and the moire field that grew from it is broad. As someone who works with superconducting devices, I find the cross-laboratory robustness of the phases more convincing than the open pairing question is troubling. The citation names the prediction and the observed phases and says nothing about a pairing mechanism, which addresses the maturity concern directly. The same three names appear in all five supporting configurations, so the allocation is stable.
statement.case_against: The credit is still not perfectly separable. Eva Andrei's STM work on flat-band localisation in twisted graphene is a legitimate parallel claim, and Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, is excluded by the three-person cap. On the chair's question, my recollection is that Andrei's results showed strongly localised states near the Dirac point in twisted graphene. They did not locate the magic-angle flat band quantitatively and did not show correlated or superconducting states, so I would not displace MacDonald, Bistritzer or Jarillo-Herrero for her. That is a memory-based judgement, the dates should be checked by outside experts, and they may decide differently. The pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder remain open, and a committee could reasonably wait a few years. I do not find that persuasive, since the prize rewards the phenomena, and waiting makes the priority picture harder to defend, not easier.

responses.point: Eriksson asked whether I could accept B014 as my first choice if circuit QED is judged too close to the 2025 prize, which he chaired.
responses.response: Yes, and I have already done so. B014 is my preferred configuration and I am no longer arguing for B046. Your point about 2025 is fair, because the macroscopic tunnelling prize covered the quantum behaviour of the circuits, and a large part of the circuit QED impact comes through processor architecture. On the Andrei and Cao question, I think the committee should say plainly in its reasoning that the three credited people are chosen for the prediction and for the discovery of the correlated phases, and that Andrei's work supports the flat-band picture without anticipating those phases.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B014 last because of the unsettled superconducting mechanism and sample variability, and prefers the lattice clock, with reservations about overlap with the frequency-comb prize.
responses.response: The chair asked what evidence would move you, so here is what I would offer from the device side. The insulating states and the superconducting dome have been reproduced by several independent groups with different probes. As I understand it, the variability concerns the critical temperature, the exact filling and the angle window, not the existence of the phases. A citation without a mechanism sidesteps the problem. On B013, I agree that the clock is a clean and cross-checked result. I still read it as a measurement capability built on the comb and ion-clock lineage, and I would keep it as an alternative but not put it ahead of a result that opens a new regime.

responses.point: Mehlig would reconsider B046 only if circuit QED can be shown to be separable in scientific content from the 2025 recognition, and warned that a two-part prize would dilute B014.
responses.response: I cannot make that case credibly, because I should not be the one advocating B046 given my position at Chalmers and in WACQT. In content, the regime of strong tunable coupling between a single artificial atom and a single photon is distinct from macroscopic tunnelling, but the committee has reasonable grounds to treat the two as one superconducting-circuit story in the prize record, and Girvin and Devoret add a credit problem. On your second point I agree. I did not propose B013 as a second part in round 1 and I still do not: both are strong, but a combined prize dilutes the single best-supported case, and B013 can be considered separately in another year.

responses.point: The chair proposes IceCube (Halzen) with the lattice clock and conceded that the single credited name is the weakest attribution on the table.
responses.response: I defer to you and Danielsson on the astroparticle science, and I accept the observational case for the diffuse flux. I cannot support B016 as a prize part unless outside experts name a defensible set that includes more than Halzen, and your own file says much the same. Without B016 your configuration reduces to the clock alone, which Kroll and Lindroth already hold. I would ask whether you could accept B014 as your lead, given that it is already your first alternative.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the lattice clock first, applies the same prior-prize overlap argument to her own candidate that she applies to circuit QED, and doubts that the interpretation of twisted bilayer graphene is stable.
responses.response: I appreciate that you apply the overlap argument to your own candidate. I think the clock is somewhat more exposed than you suggest, because the 2005 and 2012 prizes are adjacent to it in method, whereas B014 has no neighbour in the prize record. On interpretation, the flat-band mechanism that the prediction addresses is not in dispute. What is open is how the correlations and pairing arise, which the citation does not claim. If the committee prefers to wait for the SI second, B013 will remain available afterwards, but the twisted-graphene priority questions will not get easier to settle with time.

uncertainties: Whether outside experts will judge Andrei's STM flat-band work to be independent and decisive enough to change the credited set; my view that it corroborates the flat band without anticipating the correlated phases rests on memory of the literature.
Whether Yuan Cao's role as first author, outside the three-person cap, should lead the committee to reconsider the credit within B014.
Whether the open pairing mechanism will make enough members see B014 as premature that a configuration with the clock is the one that can obtain a majority.
Whether the Halzen-only credit for B016 can be repaired, which affects the chair's configuration and not mine.
statement.conflict_note: I am director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and a theorist in superconducting circuits at Chalmers, so I have a specific connection to B046 (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf) and to the wider superconducting-circuit community, including collaboration and shared meetings. I recuse myself from any final vote or advocacy on B046, and I no longer list it among my alternatives so that my proximity does not shape the ballot. In answer to the chair's question, B046 is not in my preferred configuration and I will not argue its separability from 2025. I have no specific connection to B014, B013 or B041 beyond the general quantum-physics community.
